summary_paragraph: A 52-year-old female with a complex medical history including systemic lupus erythematosus, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, common variable immunodeficiency, and prior gastric polyps was admitted for left knee and shoulder pain and swelling. She was diagnosed with septic arthritis in both joints caused by Staphylococcus lugdunensis, confirmed by joint fluid cultures. She underwent surgical washout of the left knee and shoulder. During her hospitalization, she developed ongoing gastrointestinal bleeding from pyloric polyps, which could not be definitively controlled endoscopically, leading to the discontinuation of clopidogrel to reduce bleeding risk. She also experienced transient hyperkalemia with bradycardia, requiring brief CCU care, and was found to have poor distal perfusion in the left leg due to severe peripheral artery disease. Her infection improved with IV cefazolin, and she was transitioned to an extended care facility for completion of a six-week antibiotic course, ongoing anemia management, and monitoring for recurrent bleeding or vascular complications.
